findings.title: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) did not ensure that all easement violations were resolved in a timely manner.
findings.description: MALPF did not ensure that all easement violation were resolved in a timely manner. As of June 30, 2013, there were 348 unresolved violations, including 49 high-priority ones remaining for up to seven years. Reviews and follow-up actions are not documented despite policy requirements.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that MALPF a. perform appropriate and timely follow-up actions on outstanding easement violations to ensure corrective actions were taken (repeat); b. document periodic reviews of the database and related follow-up actions; and c. determine the status of the aforementioned unresolved violations and impose penalties, if deemed appropriate (repeat).

extraction.agency_response_summary: MALPF concurs with the findings regarding follow-up actions on easement violations and documentation. The agency notes that civil penalties are a last resort and outlines steps taken, including requiring documentation of all contacts and holding bi-annual meetings with Assistant Attorneys General.
